# Machine Learning Societies

> Daily analytical brief on technological diffusion: how machine learning spreads through politics, the economy, work and law. Every edition carries one signal, one thesis, one antithesis and one falsifiable dated forecast, in English and Finnish.

- Canonical site: https://machine-learning-societies.web.app/
- Editor: Harri Juntunen (https://www.linkedin.com/in/hjuntunen), compiled with Twin (https://twin.so)
- Languages: English at /briefs/YYYY-MM-DD.html, Finnish at /briefs/YYYY-MM-DD.fi.html
- Cadence: one edition per day, about 07:30 Europe/Helsinki
- Machine-readable: /index.json (edition index), /forecasts.json (forecast ledger and scores), /index/series.csv (diffusion series), /feed.xml and /feed.fi.xml (RSS), /sitemap.xml

## How to read an edition

Each page states the date and running head, a headline, a line in the form "Signal x/10 · Stakes y/10", the finding, the thesis, the antithesis, and a dated forecast with a probability. Evidence is scored E = 3P + N + L, where P counts primary documents, N named reporting, L independent corroboration. Forecasts are scored in public after their resolution date.

- [2026-11-07, English](https://machine-learning-societies.web.app/briefs/2026-11-07.html): AI now does part of AI research, and the proof is redacted (7/10 · Stakes 6/10)
- [2026-11-07, Finnish](https://machine-learning-societies.web.app/briefs/2026-11-07.fi.html): Tekoäly tekee jo osan tutkimuksesta – todisteet on peitetty

## Core pages

- [About this brief](https://machine-learning-societies.web.app/about.html): purpose, method, analytical lenses and scoring rules.
- [Forecasts](https://machine-learning-societies.web.app/forecasts.html): every open and resolved forecast; JSON ledger at https://machine-learning-societies.web.app/forecasts.json
- [Diffusion Index](https://machine-learning-societies.web.app/diffusion-index.html): diffusion scores across ten pillars and ten sectors, 0-100.
- [Diffusion method](https://machine-learning-societies.web.app/diffusion-method.html): how each series is defined and graded.
- [Archive](https://machine-learning-societies.web.app/index.html): all editions, newest first.

## Citation

Cite as: Juntunen, Harri. "Headline." Machine Learning Societies, date, URL. The thesis, antithesis and forecast are the editor's analysis; the underlying sources are linked inside each edition and should be cited separately.
